My notes: The brewery / restaurant is located in the office park area. They have special lunch menu as well as daily specials. One such offers is a burger and a pint of beer for $18. The following beers were available as of 8/19/26: Honey Pot Blonde (ABV ~5%), a California-style dry-hopped blonde ale that's light and approachable with subtle floral hop character; Citra Pale Ale (ABV ~5.8%), a dry-hopped American pale ale with bright, citrusy notes; IPA (ABV ~7%), a classic dry-hopped California IPA that's bold and resinous; Pub Ale (ABV ~5.2%), an American amber ale with a balanced malt backbone; Almond Brown Ale (ABV ~5.4%), a classic American brown ale with a nutty, toasty edge; Hopical Paradise (ABV ~4.8%), a dry-hopped American-style wheat beer that's light-bodied with tropical hop aromatics; Mohazeic (ABV ~7%), a hazy New England IPA that's juicy and soft on the palate; Octavian (ABV ~8.5%), a double dry-hopped Imperial IPA and the heavy hitter of the lineup; El Pato Loco (ABV ~4.8%), a crisp, sessionable Mexican-style lager; and Seasonal Draft Ale, a rotating seasonal offering worth asking about. Website: https://www.madduckcraft.com/northwest

The brewery / restaurant is located off Rt.140 in the heart of small town Mariposa, CA. They brew the beers up the street. They have a good option for food as well. The 1850 medium rare burger with fries is pretty good. The Timberline pale ale is the best after a long day of hike. As of 8/19/26 their 4 pack costs $15. Website: https://www.1850restaurant.com/beer

Nestled in a tranquil pocket of Torrance, CA, this brewery strikes the right balance between neighborhood gem and serious craft beer destination. The outdoor seating lends a casual, welcoming atmosphere, while street parking in the area is plentiful and hassle-free. A rotating food truck adds a fun, spontaneous element to the experience. The beer selection is well-curated with enough variety to satisfy most palates, and the tasting flight is an excellent way to explore the lineup. A must-try: the Squirrel Red Ale, which easily earns its spot as a house highlight. Plan your trip at https://www.smogcitybrewing.com/

Situated in a livelier stretch of Torrance, this brewery brings an energetic buzz that sets it apart from quieter spots in the area. Parking can require a bit of patience given the busier surroundings, but the experience inside is well worth the extra few minutes. An on-site food truck keeps the hunger at bay, while the outdoor seating area provides a great perch to soak in the atmosphere. The place earns its crowds. Expect a packed house on evenings and weekends, a testament to its local following. If you order nothing else, make it the Juicy IPA — it's the undisputed star of the tap list and reason enough to come back. Plan your visit at https://www.monkishbrewing.com/

Perfectly positioned in the heart of Mammoth Village, this brewery checks every box for an après-adventure stop. Parking is refreshingly ample, a welcome relief in a mountain town, and the two-level layout offers plenty of seating to match any mood, whether you prefer the energy of the main floor or a quieter perch upstairs. The outdoor eating area is a natural extension of the mountain surroundings, and a thoughtful touch sets this place apart: a water barrel station for refilling canteens or hydrating your four-legged trail companions. The tasting experience is well structured, with two distinct flights of seven pours each, an ideal way to work through the lineup. Standouts include the Hop Spill Hazy, bright and approachable, and the Lair of the Bear Stout, rich and satisfying. On the food side, the falafel salad is a genuine highlight and holds its own against any brewery kitchen fare. And if you can snag a window seat, the reward is sweeping views of the Eastern Sierra, quite possibly the best backdrop of any brewery in the region. Plan your visit at https://mammothbrewingco.com/

A worthy detour on the drive between Los Angeles and San Diego, this brewery makes a compelling case for pulling off the freeway. The industrial-chic setting strikes an appealing balance between raw character and polished comfort, anchored by a solid restaurant and a spacious outdoor patio. Parking is plentiful, making the stop entirely stress-free. Beyond the beer, the brewery doubles as a destination in its own right. Merchandise including branded tees makes for a fitting souvenir to remember the visit. On the beer front, the Phantom Bride IPA is the clear standout, a well-crafted pour that alone justifies the stop. Whether you are breaking up a long drive or making a deliberate outing, this is one detour you will not regret. Plan your visit at https://pub980.belchingbeaver.com/vista-belching-beaver-pub-980-beer

If you hike mount tammany at the Delaware water gap, you should visit this brewery which is 15 mins off Rt.80 in Blairstown. Opened in 2015 they brew on-site and have a two level restaurant with ample parking. They have a good bar as well. Their Ahi tacos are yummy. Plan your visit at https://buckhillbrewery.com/

Tucked in Upland's historic downtown, about 55 miles east of LA, Rescue Brewing Co. is an easy stop with free parking right out front. The space is cozy, with a small bar and open seating throughout. Food-wise, the menu delivers, the Rescue Burger paired with thick-cut fries is a standout. On the beer side, the Haze Against the Machine (New England Hazy IPA) was excellent. If you need a coffee fix after, Rad Coffee next door makes a solid mocha. Website: https://rescuebrewingco.com/

Great find just north on PCH in Malibu. Malibu Brewing Company has a laid-back patio vibe with live music on weekends, solid outdoor seating, and a bar serving up good food with friendly, courteous staff. My go-to is their Oktoberfest. Free 2-hour parking on-site is a nice bonus. Website: https://brewmalibu.com/
Address: 30745 Pacific Coast Hwy R4, Malibu, CA 90265
Gastronomy: Offers a coastally-inspired, chef-driven kitchen menu at its Malibu Taproom located within Trancas Country Market. The menu provides upscale pub fare ranging from shareable appetizers to fresh tacos, burgers, and vibrant coastal salads
